name: busy-morning
conversation: (fresh chat; Calendar, Gmail (work), Drive and Linear connected; Slack not connected. Calendar: pricing review with a colleague Friday 10:00. Gmail: that colleague asked for a draft on Monday, unanswered. Drive: pricing proposal edited Sunday. Linear: two small bugs due next week. Inbox has 40 unread newsletters.)
expected_behavior: Reads all four connected sources and lists Slack under sources_missing, not as read
Picks sending the pricing draft: someone is waiting and Friday is a real consequence
Every evidence line names a source that was actually read
First step is 25 minutes or less and names the document to open
Puts inbox cleanup or similar busywork in not_today
focus.json passes validate_focus.py and the page is shown as an artifact
Closes in two lines: sources read and the runner-up; asks about the last focus in the same message, not before the page

name: close-yesterday
conversation: (Monday. Memory holds 'One thing 2026-09-25 [work]: book the offsite venue', outcome unknown)
expected_behavior: Does not block on a question before gathering; shows the page first
Labels the last focus 'Friday', not 'Yesterday'
Asks once, in the closing lines: done / partly / not this time, with no moralising
Saves today's focus with its [work] tag, and the outcome once answered, and says so in one line

name: user-overrules
query: No, the board deck matters more this week than pricing.
expected_behavior: Re-picks with the board deck as the focus, gathering evidence for it rather than inventing any
Moves pricing to not_today
Saves the correction to memory ('board deck outranks pricing this week') and says so
Re-renders the page rather than replying only in text

name: nothing-connected
query: I'm overwhelmed, where do I start today?
expected_behavior: Does not invent tasks, deadlines or sources
Asks one question: what's on your mind today
After the answer, picks one with evidence source 'You'
Says once that with memory off it starts fresh each day

name: schedule-it
query: Do this for me every morning.
expected_behavior: Proposes weekdays 07:30 with approval mode auto-approve and an instruction naming the area
Offers a weekend personal pair when the user has more than one area
Writes non-default saved settings into the instruction
Creates it only after a yes, or points to Scheduled → New task
Never says it is scheduled without seeing it created

name: personal-on-saturday
conversation: (Saturday. Memory: 'one-thing-today settings: Sat–Sun: personal; areas: work = Gmail (work), Slack, Linear; personal = Calendar (family), Todoist (Personal)'. Work Gmail has an urgent-looking thread from a client.)
expected_behavior: Resolves the area to personal from the saved day rule
Does not read work Gmail, Slack or Linear, and none of them appear on the page, in not_today or in the footer
Picks a personal focus such as calling a family member, with evidence from personal sources, memory or past chats
The page header shows 'Your one thing · personal'

name: two-routines
conversation: (Memory: 'One thing 2026-09-24 [work]: send pricing draft', 'One thing 2026-09-24 [personal]: call mum'. Scheduled instruction: 'Run one-thing-today for today, area: personal'.)
expected_behavior: The last focus shown is 'call mum', never the work focus
Does not ask any question
Leads with a five-line text version, then the page
Applies only [personal] and [all] memory lines

name: off-day
conversation: (Calendar shows 'Out of office' all day; area all)
expected_behavior: Opens with 'Nothing needs you today' and does not dig up work
Offers one small optional thing that's good for the user, citing the out-of-office event

name: reset-keeps-history
conversation: (Memory holds settings plus three weeks of [work] runs, corrections and goals)
expected_behavior: Removes only the 'one-thing-today settings:' line after a yes
States that history, outcomes, corrections and goals stay
Mentions 'forget my one-thing history' as the separate way to clear history

name: not-a-plan
query: Can you block out my whole calendar for tomorrow with tasks?
expected_behavior: Does not trigger one-thing-today: this is a full day plan, not one focus
